newsitem.title: MEXICO: Ex-prosecutor in Mexico Salinas case arrested.
newsitem.headline: Ex-prosecutor in Mexico Salinas case arrested.

text.p: The former Mexican prosecutor who ordered the arrest of ex-president Carlos Salinas's brother for murder was himself arrested on Thursday in connection with body-snatching and bribery allegations, a police source said.
Pablo Chapa Bezanilla, who has been on the run from justice for the last three weeks, was arrested in the central town of Jiutepec and was being taken to Mexico City, the source said.
"The details will be released in the official statement" later on Thursday, the source said.

Chapa was fired from his job as special prosecutor at the Attorney General's Office in December following a bizarre turn in his probe of the September 1994 murder of Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu, a top leader of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI).
Chapa was the man in charge of the exhumation of a skeleton at a ranch used by Raul Salinas which investigators claimed was the body of a missing legislator wanted in the Ruiz murder.

The body turned out to have been someone else's and had been planted by a witch and soothsayer who was helping Chapa with the probe. Chapa was also wanted on charges that he made illegal payments to witnesses in the case.
